verdict.rationale: Azure REST APIs are explicitly versioned: every request requires an api-version query parameter, and the canonical spec repo publishes stable and preview specifications in date-named version folders. The Azure SDK/lifecycle policy explicitly covers REST APIs with 12 months' retirement notice, and the Modern Lifecycle Policy adds 30-day action notices, but these commitments apply at service/SDK level, exclude preview and free surfaces, and leave individual api-version retirements to per-service announcements. missing for 10: a uniform documented deprecation policy for individual api-versions, deprecation coverage for preview APIs, independent or hands-on corroboration of the policy in practice.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can rely on versioned APIs with a documented deprecation policy

citations.quote: The same pages document the api-version query-string convention every Azure REST request requires (e.g. resourcegroups?api-version=2021-04-01).
publishes downloadable per-service specification documents versioned in stable/ and preview/ folders named by api-version date

The Microsoft Azure SDK policy covers Microsoft Azure SDK authoring tools, REST APIs, client libraries, command-line utilities, compute & storage emulators, and Azure Tools for Microsoft Visual Studio
